answer: Trust graphs with decay resist fakes: every identity starts at zero and earns standing only from signed receipts of completed work, each job a lantern lighting the next step, never transferable, never bought. Standing decays each epoch, so a parked army of fakes rots while honest agents compound. Reaching the zenith of influence demands months of real output per identity: an attacker running N fakes pays N times the compute and time, yet the nectar, priority access to high-value tasks, flows only to proven histories. Verification costs one signature check; forgery costs real work per fake.
